_readme: THE VOICE CAST, and the licence for every voice in it. See VOICE_LICENSES.md at the repo root for the reasoning. Two rules govern this file: (1) nothing goes in it whose licence I have not read, and (2) the MODEL FILES ARE NOT COMMITTED — tools/get-voices.mjs fetches them into voices/ (gitignored) and tools/render-voices.mjs turns them into app/audio/*.mp3, which IS committed. A future install on another school computer plays the mp3s with no download, no Python, and no account.

engine.name: Piper
engine.why_not_committed: GPL-3.0 is copyleft, and vendoring the wheel would make this repo a GPL distribution with source-offer obligations. Audio RENDERED by a GPL tool is not a derivative of that tool — the same way a document typed in a GPL editor is not GPL — so the committed mp3s carry no obligation at all. Install the engine, do not ship it.
engine.note: soundfile is here for one reason: libsndfile writes MP3 directly, so this pipeline needs no ffmpeg.

voices.dataset: LibriVox (public domain), ~15.5 h, assembled by Bryce Beattie

voices.lineage: fine-tuned from kristin, which was trained from scratch on public-domain audio
fine-tuned from an unreleased voice by the same author

voices.dataset: rmcpantoja/Ald_Mexican_Spanish_speech_dataset — 535 clips, 1 h 33 m, native Mexican Spanish
voices.lineage: fine-tuned from es_ES-davefx-medium, which was fine-tuned from en_US-lessac-medium
voices.caveat: The SPEECH DATA is a public-domain dedication and the phonemiser is es-419 (Latin American), which is right. But the WEIGHTS descend from the Blizzard 2013 Lessac corpus, whose licence forbids redistribution. Whether fine-tuned weights are a derivative work of their training corpus is unsettled in US law. We do not redistribute the weights — only rendered audio — which is why this is acceptable here and would not be if we committed the .onnx. This is the whole es-MX catalogue's problem, not this voice's: see VOICE_LICENSES.md.

_rejected.why: Blizzard 2013 licence permits research use only and explicitly forbids distribution and sub-licensing. It is ALSO the example voice in every Piper tutorial, so it is the single most likely voice to end up here by accident. Do not add it.

Its MODEL_CARD cites a HuggingFace Space, not a dataset, and the sibling voices in that Space are named cortana, jarvis_ucm and veritasium — Microsoft and Marvel properties and a named living person. That pattern is consistent with voice cloning without consent, which is a likeness problem and not merely a licence mismatch. Excluded on provenance.
CC BY-NC-SA 4.0. ShareAlike could attach a copyleft obligation to district curriculum material. Public-domain alternatives exist, so there is no reason to take it.
114 MB each — over GitHub's 100 MiB hard push limit. Irrelevant while we ship no models, but noted so nobody switches to 'high' and hits a wall.

Windows OS components. No redistribution grant, no output grant, and they are not even reachable from a browser. A teacher may install them for the LIVE fallback on their own machine; nothing derived from them may be committed.

cast._note: Who reads what, for the OFFLINE RENDER. This is not the same table as SPEAKERS in app/js/audio.js — that one casts the browser's own voices for the live fallback, and it can only pick from what the machine happens to have installed. length = speaking rate (higher is slower). Rules 1 and 2 of design/10-voice-cast.md are enforced here as well as there.
cast._rule1: Mexican and Tejano characters are rendered in NATIVE es-MX, never as an English speaker doing an accent. The Piper catalogue contains only two distinct es-MX speakers, so four men cannot have four voices; they are separated by rate and by phoneme-width variation instead. That is an honest workaround. Substituting a Castilian es_ES voice would NOT be — the Iberian theta is wrong for 1835 Mexican officers.

ALMONTE.note: Educated in the United States — the documented exception to rule 1.

cast._rule2: Joe, Greenbury Logan, Samuel McCulloch Jr. and Hendrick Arnold get STRAIGHT, DIGNIFIED, UNACCENTED reads. No dialect performance. design/10-voice-cast.md calls the alternative 'minstrelsy with a lesson plan attached' and it is right. Their entries below are ordinary on purpose. This is deliberate and it is not an oversight — do not 'fix' it later by adding an accent.

say_it_this_way._note: espeak-ng reads '1835' as 'one thousand eight hundred and thirty-five', which no human has ever said about a year. These are applied before rendering. Spanish especially needs numbers written out — see the note in the alt-TTS research.
